item.title: Go Daily Question 123
item.description:
What does the following code print, and why?

package main

import (
 "fmt"
)

type People interface {
 Show()
}

type Student struct{}

func (stu *Student) Show() {

}

func live() People {
 var stu *Student
 return stu
}

func main() {
 if live() == nil {
 fmt.Println("AAAAAAA")
 } else {
 fmt.Println("BBBBBBB")
 }
}
🔑 Answer Analysis:

Answer: BBBBBBB Simply put, an interface variable has two values: one is its type, and the other is its value. For an if interface, the live() == nil condition is true only when both the value and the type are zero values.
